note: Demo (Chinh). Raw factor values on the docs/INTERFACES.md section 8 grid.
cell: each pixel = its 120 m cell with the best combined score; all layers from the same cell
combine: equal weights; any factor scoring 0 makes the combined score 0; missing data left out

factors.name: Landing slope
factors.source: "Surface slope for landing (100m): <10 deg" (NASA, Artemis Human Landing System Update (2024), NTRS 20240009596). Measured across 120 m, steepest side.
factors.explain: How steep the ground is right under the lander. Over 10 deg it may tip over.

factors.name: Walk-out slope
factors.source: "Surface slope limit for EVA (2km): <20 deg" (NASA, Artemis Human Landing System Update (2024), NTRS 20240009596). Grade over a ~2 km baseline.
factors.explain: How steep the way out is over the 2 km astronauts can walk. Over 20 deg they cannot walk out.

factors.name: Bowl / crater floor
factors.source: Team assumption: 70 m below the mean ground within 2 km is ground rising about 2 deg on every side.
factors.explain: How far the spot sits below the average ground within 2 km. Crater floors are darker, colder and hard to leave.

factors.name: Sunlight
factors.source: NASA GSFC PGDA long-run average (product 69). Reject at 30 % is a team assumption.
factors.explain: Share of time the Sun is up over the terrain, averaged over 18.6 years. Power and warmth.

factors.name: Earth in view
factors.source: NASA GSFC PGDA long-run average (product 69). Reject at 30 % is a team assumption.
factors.explain: Share of time Earth is above the skyline, so the radio can reach home without a relay.

factors.name: Distance to ice
factors.source: Permanent shadow = PGDA sunlight 0 over at least 1 km2 (team choice, as docs/criteria.md). 10 km reject: team assumption.
factors.explain: How far to the nearest permanently shadowed ground, where water ice can survive.

factors.name: Ground temperature
factors.source: LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product. 110 K: "surfaces below 110 K capable of cold trapping water" (Williams et al. 2019).
factors.explain: Yearly mean temperature just below the surface. Colder ground needs more heater power.

factors.name: Buried ice depth
factors.source: LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product (ice stability depth, thermal model). 1 m reject: team assumption.
factors.explain: How deep you would have to dig before water ice could stay frozen. Shallower is easier to reach.
